inspiration: Threat is applied in one ordered pass: spell-attribute gate, then threat modifiers, then redirect share, then combat check, then add to an existing entry or create one, then victim update (ThreatManager.cpp lines 382-476). Use this order as the hate-list step for row 4: gate, modify, split, check, apply, update target.

Threat by school is multiplied by the defender's own school modifiers, not the attacker's (CalculateModifiedThreat, ThreatManager.cpp lines 677-714; the normal-school line is 696). This is the closest thing in the box to 'threat scales with protection': a defender with more protection in one school draws more or less hate from hits in that school. Recreate with our own schools and numbers.

Entries go offline when the target can no longer be seen, attacked or fought (ShouldBeOffline, ThreatManager.cpp lines 99-109). They come back when the target is visible again. Use this for row 4 leash and aggro: lost sight drops the target off the hate list, sight re-adds it.
Suppression is a separate state from offline: an immune, confused or stunned target is suppressed, and a taunting target is never suppressed (ShouldBeSuppressed, lines 110-121; taunt check line 112).

Victim re-evaluation runs on a fixed one-second timer (ThreatManager::Update lines 215-231; THREAT_UPDATE_INTERVAL = 1000u at ThreatManager.h line 86), and a brand-new entry triggers an immediate victim update (end of AddThreat). Use for the server tick budget (post-K item 3): cheap timer check each tick, immediate update only when the list changes.

Spawn data is per row: each spawn has a respawn time in seconds and a pool id, and each spawn group has flags for dynamic spawn rate and despawn on condition failure (SpawnData.h lines 53-61 and 133-142). Map straight onto row 23: cap through pool, respawn seconds per row, despawn when a condition fails.

briefs.label: Hate Ward (own label)
briefs.why: A defender whose school state changes how much hate its hits generate creates a readable tank-or-glass choice without any new combat rule. The player sees the change as a ring colour, not a number.
briefs.keep: threat multiplied by the defender's school state; hits in a school the defender is warded against draw different hate
briefs.change: our state is an armour stance or a shield tier, not a school table; the ward is shown as a band of colour on the defender; the numbers are our own zone data

briefs.label: Ambush Pocket (own label)
briefs.why: A spawn group that despawns when its condition fails (for example, the player leaves the pocket) keeps a zone from filling up with stale enemies, and a dynamic spawn rate lets a quiet zone wake up.
briefs.keep: a spawn group as one unit with flags; despawn on condition failure; spawn rate that changes with activity
briefs.change: our group is named and gated by our own zone triggers; the rate curve and cap are zone data fields; no copy of the donor's flag names
